query: A matrix has rank zero exactly when every entry is zero.
For a Hermitian matrix, strict positivity of every eigenvalue is equivalent to positive definiteness.
A Hermitian matrix is positive semidefinite if and only if all its eigenvalues are nonnegative; zero eigenvalues are allowed.
Characterize a positive definite matrix by its Hermitian symmetry and strictly positive energy on every nonzero vector.
Characterize a positive semidefinite matrix by Hermitian symmetry and a nonnegative quadratic form on every vector.
Multiplying the right hand side by the Moore Penrose inverse gives a least squares solution, even if the matrix is rank deficient.
Among all vectors minimizing the residual, the solution computed by the pseudoinverse has the smallest Euclidean length.
Taking the generalized inverse twice recovers the original matrix.
The operator two norm of a product of rectangular matrices is at most the product of their operator two norms.
Bound the Frobenius norm of A times B using the spectral norm of A and the Frobenius norm of B.
Bound the Frobenius norm of A times B using the Frobenius norm of A and the spectral norm of B.
The trace norm of a rectangular matrix is the real trace of the positive square root of its adjoint times itself.
The Schatten norm with exponent two agrees with the Frobenius norm.
Weyl's inequality bounds an ordered eigenvalue of the sum of two Hermitian matrices by the sum of two ordered eigenvalues of the summands.
Changing a Hermitian matrix by a small operator norm perturbation moves each ordered eigenvalue by at most that amount.
Two matrices have the same orthogonal projector exactly when their column spaces agree, even if they have different numbers of columns.
The Moore Penrose inverse multiplied on the right by the original matrix is the orthogonal projector onto the row space.
Keeping the leading singular components gives a Frobenius error no worse than any other matrix of rank at most k.
The spectral norm error after retaining k singular values equals the first discarded singular value.
The squared Frobenius error of singular value truncation is the sum of the squares of the discarded singular values.
For two orthonormal bases of subspaces, the singular values of their cross Gram matrix are the cosines of the principal angles.
For two subspaces of equal positive dimension, the operator norm distance between their orthogonal projectors equals the sine of their largest principal angle.
